result:
Ran `git gc`. `.git` went from 144K → 110K; the 35 loose objects (25.8 KiB) are now a single 15.5 KiB pack.

There wasn't much to reclaim — this checkout is tiny, no stashes, no unreachable objects, and nothing dangling in the reflog, so `gc` was purely a repack. I didn't use `--prune=now` or `--aggressive` since there was nothing unreachable to prune and no measurable win at this size.

One thing worth flagging separately: commit `5fbf7d8 config: add service token` still holds that token in reachable history (`c5daf92` only removed it going forward). `gc` cannot touch it — that would need a history rewrite (`git filter-repo`) plus rotating the token. Say the word if you want that.
